language.script_notes: Strong regional dialects (Neapolitan, Sicilian) sometimes appear on informal signage.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Common on winding coastal roads (Amalfi Coast).
road_furniture.curb_style: Narrow, winding roads through hill towns; less formal shoulder/curb infrastructure than the industrial north.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Generally less dense motorway signage than the north.

architecture.roof_style: Flatter, low-pitch roofs common in the deep south and Sicily reflecting drier climate; terracotta pitched roofs still standard elsewhere.
architecture.wall_construction: Whitewashed cave-dwelling architecture (sassi) in Matera; pastel-painted hill towns (e.g. Ostuni's 'White Town') in Puglia; dense, weathered stone/stucco construction in Naples; baroque architecture in Sicilian towns (Noto, Ragusa) rebuilt after the 1693 earthquake.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Whitewash and pastel tones dominate coastal towns; warm sun-bleached ochre and cream in inland hill towns; dramatic dark volcanic stone near Mount Etna in Sicily.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Whitewashed cave dwellings (sassi di Matera); pastel hill towns; trulli — distinctive conical dry-stone huts unique to Puglia; dense, vertical Naples streetscapes; Sicilian baroque towns; Mount Etna's volcanic backdrop.

nature.vegetation: Mediterranean evergreen scrub (macchia), olive groves, holm oak, umbrella pines and citrus orchards dominate; prickly pear cactus common in Sicily and Puglia; noticeably drier and browner in summer than the north.
nature.terrain: Dramatic coastlines (Amalfi Coast, Cinque Terre further north but similar style, Sicilian coast); the Apennines continue south; Mount Etna's active volcanic cone dominates eastern Sicily; flatter plains in Puglia.
nature.climate_signature: Classic sun-bleached Mediterranean light, hot dry summers, sparse golden-brown vegetation by late summer — a warmer, brighter look than the hazy north.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Smaller, older cars and scooters (Vespa/Piaggio) proportionally more common than in the wealthier industrial north.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 4 in cities and along the coast; some older/lower coverage in remote inland hill towns.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coastal and city coverage; noticeably thinner in remote inland mountain areas of Basilicata/Calabria/interior Sicily than the industrial north.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script, same plate and bollard style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The south has Mediterranean scrub, olive groves, pastel/whitewashed hill towns and a sun-bleached coastal light; the north has flat cultivated Po Valley farmland, foggy continental winters and Alpine peaks.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar Mediterranean whitewashed architecture, bright coastal light, olive groves
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Italy uses Latin script and Italian vocabulary ('Via', 'Piazza') vs. Greek script and language; Italy's bollard/plate design differs from Greece's.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar Mediterranean limestone architecture and climate near Sicily
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Malta drives on the LEFT (former British colony) with UK-style road signage; Sicily/southern Italy drives on the right with standard Italian signage.
